### Problem: Range Sum Query 2D – Mutable {#sec-sqrt-p1-mutable2d}

::: {.p-statement}
Maintain an $m \times n$ integer matrix and answer two operations, interleaved:

- `update(row, col, val)` — set $\mathit{matrix}[\mathit{row}][\mathit{col}] = \mathit{val}$;
- `sumRegion(r_1, c_1, r_2, c_2)` — return the sum of the sub-matrix with corners $(r_1,c_1)$ and $(r_2,c_2)$, inclusive.

Constraints: $0 \le m, n \le 200$, $-10^{5} \le \mathit{matrix}[i][j], \mathit{val} \le 10^{5}$, up to $10^{5}$ operations combined.

Source: [LC 308 · Range Sum Query 2D - Mutable](https://leetcode.com/problems/range-sum-query-2d-mutable/){.solved difficulty="Hard"}

Example — with $\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\3&4\end{bmatrix}$: `sumRegion(0,0,1,1) = 10`; `update(0,0,5)`; `sumRegion(0,0,0,1) = 7`; `sumRegion(1,0,1,1) = 7`. (Every number below is asserted, and the block answers are stressed against a raw nested-loop oracle.)
:::

::: {.p-intuition}
The static 2D prefix table (LC 304) answers `sumRegion` in $O(1)$ but costs $O(mn)$ to rebuild after any `update`. Block one axis — the **rows** — into strips of $B=\sqrt{m}$. For each row-strip keep a column-prefix of the strip's column sums, so "sum of rows $[bB, bB{+}B)$ and columns $[c_1,c_2]$" is one $O(1)$ subtraction. A query adds whole strips by their strip-prefix and the $\le 2B$ leftover rows by their own row-prefix — $O(m/B + B) = O(\sqrt m)$. An `update` rebuilds exactly one strip and one row's prefix. This is @sec-sqrt-a1's walk with the blocks laid along the row axis and the "summary" promoted from a single number to a column-prefix array.
:::

::: {.p-approach}
1. **Nested-loop scan.** Keep the matrix; `update` writes one cell; `sumRegion` double-loops the sub-rectangle. $O(mn)$ per query, $O(q\,mn)$ overall — the oracle.
2. **Row-blocked column prefixes.** Per-strip column prefix for the middle, per-row prefix for the edges; `update` touches one strip. $O(\sqrt m)$ query, $O(n)$ update.

**Invariant.** `pre[b][c]` = sum over strips $b$'s rows and columns $[0, c)$; `rp[r][c]` = prefix of row $r$ over columns $[0,c)$. Both are recomputed for every strip / row the `update` touches, so they always match the live matrix.
:::

The buttons are in order. Each one keeps the previous solution and changes only what that form changes.

::: {.panel-tabset .solution-forms}

#### Nested-loop scan

::: {.form-next}
Store the matrix, write one cell on `update`, and add up the rectangle cell by cell on `sumRegion`. $O(mn)$ per query — the truth we diff the blocked version against.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
class NumMatrixBrute:
    def __init__(self, matrix):
        self.mat = [list(r) for r in matrix]

    def update(self, r, c, val):
        self.mat[r][c] = val

    def sumRegion(self, r1, c1, r2, c2):
        return sum(self.mat[r][c] for r in range(r1, r2 + 1) for c in range(c1, c2 + 1))


nb = NumMatrixBrute([[1, 2], [3, 4]])
assert nb.sumRegion(0, 0, 1, 1) == 10
nb.update(0, 0, 5)
assert nb.sumRegion(0, 0, 0, 1) == 7 and nb.sumRegion(1, 0, 1, 1) == 7
```

##### C++

```cpp
// brute force: O(1) update, O(area) sumRegion
class NumMatrixBrute {
    vector<vector<long long> > a;
public:
    NumMatrixBrute(vector<vector<int> >& matrix) {
        a.assign(matrix.size(), vector<long long>(matrix.empty() ? 0 : matrix[0].size()));
        for (size_t i = 0; i < matrix.size(); ++i)
            for (size_t j = 0; j < matrix[i].size(); ++j) a[i][j] = matrix[i][j];
    }
    void update(int r, int c, int val) { a[r][c] = val; }
    long long sumRegion(int r1, int c1, int r2, int c2) {
        long long s = 0;
        for (int r = r1; r <= r2; ++r)
            for (int c = c1; c <= c2; ++c) s += a[r][c];
        return s;
    }
};
```
:::

**Reading it line by line.** The Python one-liner is deliberately clumsy to keep it obviously the definition — iterate the rows, sum each row's slice. It is the oracle, nothing more: at $10^{5}$ operations each touching $200 \times 200$ cells it is $\sim 4\cdot10^{9}$ adds. The blocked form below replaces the per-query double loop with one $O(1)$ subtraction per strip.

#### Row-blocked column prefixes

::: {.form-next}
Slice rows into strips of $B=\sqrt{m}$. Keep `pre[b]` = column-prefix of strip $b$'s per-column sums, and `rp[r]` = column-prefix of row $r$. `sumRegion` walks $r_1$ to a strip boundary by row-prefixes, adds whole strips by strip-prefix, then finishes by row-prefixes — $O(B + m/B)$ with $O(1)$ per term. `update(r,c,v)` rewrites the cell, then rebuilds row $r$'s prefix and strip $r/B$'s prefix.
:::


::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: sec-sqrt-p1-mutable2d-sol
class NumMatrix:
    def __init__(self, matrix, B=None):
        self.mat = [list(r) for r in matrix]
        self.rows = len(self.mat)
        self.cols = len(self.mat[0]) if self.rows else 0
        self.B = B or max(1, int(round(self.rows ** 0.5)))
        self.nb = (self.rows + self.B - 1) // self.B
        self.pre = [None] * self.nb          # strip column-prefix, length cols+1
        self.rp = [None] * self.rows         # per-row column-prefix, length cols+1
        for r in range(self.rows):
            self._redo_row(r)
        for b in range(self.nb):
            self._redo_strip(b)

    def _redo_row(self, r):
        acc = [0]
        for c in range(self.cols):
            acc.append(acc[-1] + self.mat[r][c])
        self.rp[r] = acc

    def _redo_strip(self, b):
        lo, hi = b * self.B, min(self.rows, (b + 1) * self.B)
        colsum = [0] * self.cols
        for r in range(lo, hi):
            for c in range(self.cols):
                colsum[c] += self.mat[r][c]
        acc = [0]
        for v in colsum:
            acc.append(acc[-1] + v)
        self.pre[b] = acc

    def update(self, r, c, val):
        self.mat[r][c] = val
        self._redo_row(r)
        self._redo_strip(r // self.B)

    def sumRegion(self, r1, c1, r2, c2):
        if self.rows == 0:
            return 0
        total = 0
        while r1 <= r2 and r1 % self.B:                     # partial rows above the first whole strip
            total += self.rp[r1][c2 + 1] - self.rp[r1][c1]; r1 += 1
        while r1 + self.B - 1 <= r2:                         # whole strips, one subtraction each
            b = r1 // self.B
            total += self.pre[b][c2 + 1] - self.pre[b][c1]; r1 += self.B
        while r1 <= r2:                                      # partial rows below
            total += self.rp[r1][c2 + 1] - self.rp[r1][c1]; r1 += 1
        return total


nm = NumMatrix([[1, 2], [3, 4]], B=1)
assert nm.sumRegion(0, 0, 1, 1) == 10
nm.update(0, 0, 5)
assert nm.sumRegion(0, 0, 0, 1) == 7 and nm.sumRegion(1, 0, 1, 1) == 7
assert NumMatrix([]).sumRegion(0, 0, 0, 0) == 0
for _ in range(120):
    m_ = random.randint(1, 12)
    n_ = random.randint(1, 12)
    mat = [[random.randint(-10**5, 10**5) for _ in range(n_)] for _ in range(m_)]
    fast = NumMatrix(mat, random.randint(1, m_))
    slow = NumMatrixBrute([list(r) for r in mat])
    for _ in range(20):
        if random.random() < 0.35:
            r, c = random.randrange(m_), random.randrange(n_)
            v = random.randint(-10**5, 10**5)
            fast.update(r, c, v); slow.update(r, c, v)
        else:
            r1, r2 = sorted((random.randrange(m_), random.randrange(m_)))
            c1, c2 = sorted((random.randrange(n_), random.randrange(n_)))
            assert fast.sumRegion(r1, c1, r2, c2) == slow.sumRegion(r1, c1, r2, c2)
```

##### C++

```cpp
class NumMatrix {
    vector<vector<long long> > a;
    vector<vector<long long> > pre;   // per-strip column prefix (cols+1)
    vector<vector<long long> > rp;    // per-row column prefix (cols+1)
    int rows, cols, B, nb;
public:
    NumMatrix(vector<vector<int> >& matrix) {
        rows = (int)matrix.size();
        cols = rows ? (int)matrix[0].size() : 0;
        a.assign(rows, vector<long long>(cols));
        for (int i = 0; i < rows; ++i)
            for (int j = 0; j < cols; ++j) a[i][j] = matrix[i][j];
        B = max(1, (int)round(sqrt((double)max(rows, 1))));
        nb = (rows + B - 1) / B;
        pre.assign(nb, vector<long long>(cols + 1, 0));
        rp.assign(rows, vector<long long>(cols + 1, 0));
        for (int r = 0; r < rows; ++r) redoRow(r);
        for (int b = 0; b < nb; ++b) redoStrip(b);
    }
    void redoRow(int r) {
        rp[r].assign(cols + 1, 0);
        for (int c = 0; c < cols; ++c) rp[r][c + 1] = rp[r][c] + a[r][c];
    }
    void redoStrip(int b) {
        int lo = b * B, hi = min(rows, (b + 1) * B);
        pre[b].assign(cols + 1, 0);
        for (int c = 0; c < cols; ++c) {
            long long colsum = 0;
            for (int r = lo; r < hi; ++r) colsum += a[r][c];
            pre[b][c + 1] = pre[b][c] + colsum;
        }
    }
    void update(int r, int c, int val) {
        a[r][c] = val;
        redoRow(r);
        redoStrip(r / B);
    }
    long long sumRegion(int r1, int c1, int r2, int c2) {
        if (rows == 0) return 0;
        long long total = 0;
        while (r1 <= r2 && r1 % B != 0) { total += rp[r1][c2 + 1] - rp[r1][c1]; ++r1; }
        while (r1 + B - 1 <= r2) { int b = r1 / B; total += pre[b][c2 + 1] - pre[b][c1]; r1 += B; }
        while (r1 <= r2) { total += rp[r1][c2 + 1] - rp[r1][c1]; ++r1; }
        return total;
    }
};
```
:::

**Reading it line by line.** The three `while`s are the @sec-sqrt-a1 edge–middle–edge walk on the **row** axis, and every term is an $O(1)$ prefix subtraction on the **column** axis — the two dimensions are handled by different devices, which is why a query is $O(\sqrt m)$ rather than $O(\sqrt{mn})$. The middle loop's guard `r1 + B - 1 <= r2` admits a strip only when all $B$ of its rows sit inside $[r_1, r_2]$; the two residual bands of $< B$ rows are paid by `rp`. `update` rebuilds one strip in $O(B \cdot n)$ (re-sum its columns) plus one row in $O(n)$; it is the "partial rebuild of the touched block" of @sec-sqrt-a3 applied once per write, and it is the honest reason this is $O(n)$ update / $O(\sqrt m)$ query, not the fully-symmetric $O(\log^2)$ of a 2D Fenwick.

:::

::: {.p-complexity}
**Nested loop:** $O(mn)$ per query. **Row-blocked:** $O(\sqrt m)$ per `sumRegion`, $O(B \cdot n) = O(\sqrt m \cdot n)$ per `update` (dominated by rebuilding one strip), $O(mn)$ memory for the strip and row prefixes. With $m=n=200$ both are a few thousand steps per operation, far under $10^{5}\cdot$(a few thousand) the naive worst case. The full-matrix sum reaches $200\cdot200\cdot10^{5}=4\cdot10^{9}$, so every accumulator is `long long` (@sec-arr-size-trap).
:::

::: {.p-edge}
- The empty matrix ($m=0$ or $n=0$): `rows == 0` short-circuits `sumRegion` to $0$; `B` is clamped to $\ge 1$ so no division by zero. Asserted.
- A query inside a single strip (no whole strip fits): both middle loop never runs; the two edge loops meet at $r_2$.
- A query one cell tall: `r1 % B` and `r1 + B - 1 <= r2` both skip the strip loop; only the row-prefix path runs.
- Column window narrower than the strip's width is irrelevant — the strip prefix subtracts at $c_1, c_2$ like any row prefix.
:::
